In the typical case (other inputs at their typical values) the exit is 0.00 at sodium 137, 0.46 at 136, 3.24 at 130 and 5.55 at 125.

A higher BMI moves the switch-on point to a lower sodium: with BMI 20 the exit is still on at sodium 138 (0.10) and off at 139; with BMI 30 it is on at 136 (0.27) and off at 137; with BMI 40 it is on at 134 (0.43) and off at 135.

On the training split the exit is positive for 495 of 1500 patients (outcome rate 30.7%, mean predicted risk 29%, against 45.1% and 46% for the rest), 406 of them among the 417 patients with sodium below 137 mmol/L.

The leaf has no edge of its own to the output: it acts through the low-sodium arm (unit 1789), which is positive on 187 of these rows (the arm needs the hinge above about one unit before it switches on, so the hinge's weakest activations do not reach the prediction).
Switching the leaf off (its exit replaced by its mean) lowers whole-model AUC from 0.857 to 0.821 and shifts the mean predicted risk by 0.036.

Concept probe: '(137 - sodium) - 0.2 * (bmi - 27)' predicts the exit with score 1.00 (grade meaningful); '137 - sodium' alone scores 0.98; the U-shaped '(sodium - 137) ** 2' scores 0.29, confirming that this leaf is the low-sodium side only.
Closed form from get_formula (coefficients to three significant figures, standardised inputs); maximum absolute error against the exact unit on the training rows 0.0091.

The exit is zero across the low and normal range and rises in a straight line above the upper end of the normal range: in the typical case it is 0.00 at sodium 141, 0.027 at 142, 0.25 at 143, 0.69 at 145 and 1.80 at 150.

The noise column shifts the switch-on point slightly: at sodium 142 the exit is 0.31 with noise -2, 0.027 with noise 0 and 0.00 with noise 2; at sodium 144 it is 0.76, 0.47 and 0.18 for the same three noise values.

Its edge into the output weighs 3.22 (the first high-sodium hinge's weighs 1.61 and the low-sodium arm's 1.40), the heaviest edge into the output, so once it is on the risk climbs fast with sodium: whole-model risk in the typical case goes from 34% at sodium 142 to 92% at 145 and above 99% at 148 (p

On the training split the exit is positive for 334 patients (outcome rate 75.7%, mean predicted risk 76%, against 30.2% and 30% for the rest); none of them has sodium below 141 mmol/L (0 such rows), and 63 have sodium of 142 or less.
Switching the leaf off lowers whole-model AUC from 0.857 to 0.839 and shifts the mean predicted risk by 0.047.
Concept probe: 'sodium - 142' predicts the exit with score 0.99 (grade meaningful); the step 'sodium > 142' scores 0.98.
Closed form from get_formula (three significant figures, standardised inputs); maximum absolute error on the training rows 0.0013.
Rows with the exit positive and sodium below 141 mmol/L (count).
On the training split the exit is positive for 365 patients: 362 non-diabetic and 3 of the 441 diabetic patients.
In a constructed low-sodium, high-noise case (sodium 130, noise 2.5) the exit is 1.70 for a non-diabetic and 0.00 for a diabetic patient, and the low-sodium arm it feeds is 1.51 against 2.11.
Its only route to the prediction is a small negative edge into the low-sodium arm, and the exit and the arm are both positive on just 7 training rows.
Switching the chain off leaves whole-model AUC at 0.8565 against 0.8565 (mean absolute risk change 0.0001): the chain is fitted noise with no practical effect.

Concept probe: the best library concept, 'sodium * noise', scores 0.79 (grade partial); 'noise' alone 0.78; the ad hoc '(sodium - 139 + 4 * noise) * (1 - diabetes)' scores 0.95 but is a restatement of the unit's own gate, not a domain concept.
Closed form from get_formula; maximum absolute error on the training rows 0.018.
On the training split exit 7171 is positive for 892 patients, 27 of the 427 with creatinine above 100 umol/L; exit 8285 is positive for 568 patients, 6 of them with creatinine above 100.
In a constructed low-sodium, high-noise case (sodium 130, noise 2.5) creatinine 50 gives exits 6.19 and 4.63, creatinine 90 gives 1.97 and 0.45, and creatinine 110 gives 0.00 and 0.00.

Both exits enter the low-sodium arm with small negative weights, so in that constructed case the arm is 0.09 and the whole-model risk 11% at creatinine 50, against 2.22 and 85% at creatinine 110 (the direct creatinine edge adds to that difference).
On the training split an exit and the arm are both positive on 83 rows (exit 7171) and 41 rows (exit 8285).
Switching the chain off changes whole-model AUC from 0.857 to 0.853 and the mean predicted risk by -0.007.
Concept probe: the best library concept is 'creatinine' with score 0.91 (grade meaningful), because the exits are gated off by high creatinine; 'noise' alone scores 0.27.
Closed form from get_formula (both exits); maximum absolute error on the training rows 0.015.
Rows with exit 7171 positive and creatinine above 100 umol/L.

On the training split the arm is positive for 187 patients (outcome rate 50.3%, mean predicted risk 49%, against 38.9% and 39% for the rest); it is never positive while the hinge is zero (0 such rows), and 12 of its rows have sodium of 135 mmol/L or more.

In the typical case the arm switches on between sodium 135 (exit 0.00) and 134 (0.026), reaching 2.41 at 130 and 5.38 at 125; the whole-model risk is 10% at sodium 137, 39% at 132, 77% at 130 and 98% at 127.

At sodium 130 smoking raises the arm's exit from 2.41 to 2.69 and diabetes to 2.82 (both: 3.10); the whole-model risk for the four cases is 77%, 93%, 92% and 98%, most of that from the direct smoker and diabetes edges in the root.
Through this arm alone the smoker edge weighs 0.122 and the diabetes edge 0.188 per standardised unit.

The noise chains pull the arm down when the noise column is high: at sodium 130, noise 1 leaves the exit at 2.41 (risk 80%) while noise 3 lowers it to 1.06 (risk 46%); switching the three chain edges off changes AUC from 0.8565 to 0.8538.
Switching the whole arm off lowers AUC from 0.857 to 0.821 and shifts the mean predicted risk by 0.036.

Parallel composition of the model's U-shaped response to serum sodium, with three exits into the output: the low-sodium arm (unit 1789, output weight 1.40), a first high-sodium hinge (unit 219, weight 1.61) and the steep high-sodium hinge (unit 1180, weight 3.22).

The first high-sodium hinge switches on just above the middle of the normal range and rises linearly with sodium, with a small extra for men: in the typical case it is 0.00 at sodium 137 for women and 0.00 for men, 0.017 and 0.14 at 138, 0.39 and 0.51 at 140, and 2.25 and 2.37 at 150; the male edge

On the training split this hinge is positive for 945 patients, including 812 of the 812 with sodium of 139 mmol/L or more and 133 of the 688 with sodium of 138 or less; it is also positive on 334 of the 334 rows where the steep hinge is positive.

The low-sodium arm also feeds the first high-sodium hinge through an edge of weight 0.0087, whose removal changes the predicted risk by 0.0002 on average (mean absolute change); with 0 training rows where both are positive, that edge is inert on the training data.

Between sodium 135 and 137 mmol/L, 316 of the 328 training patients have all three exits at zero; across the whole split 368 patients have all three at zero, with outcome rate 19.0% and mean predicted risk 19%.
The U in the typical case (whole model): risk above 99% at sodium 125, 77% at 130, 22% at 133, 10% at 135 and 10% at 137 (the floor), then 21% at 140, 59% at 143, 92% at 145 and above 99% at 150.
By sodium band on the training split: below 135 mmol/L 227 patients, outcome rate 44.1%, mean predicted risk 43%; 135 to 142, 998 patients, 28.2% and 28%; above 142, 275 patients, 81.5% and 82%.
Switching the whole composition off lowers AUC from 0.857 to 0.697 and shifts the mean predicted risk by 0.204; the first high-sodium hinge alone is worth 0.857 to 0.831.
Sodium above 142 mmol/L: n, outcome rate, mean predicted risk.

Each direct term is positive, so on its own edge each input raises the risk: per standardised unit, age weighs 0.79, BMI 0.38, creatinine 0.36, smoker 0.40, diabetes 0.28 and the noise column 0.17; switching all six off (each replaced by its mean contribution) lowers AUC from 0.857 to 0.767.
Whole-model sweeps in the typical case: age 30 gives risk 2%, age 60 15% and age 90 57%;

Systolic blood pressure and heart rate have no enabled connections and no effect: the risk is 16% at systolic pressure 90, 16% at 145 and 16% at 200 mmHg, and 16%, 16% and 16% at heart rates 50, 85 and 120.
On the training split the outcome rate is 40.3% over 1500 patients and the model's AUC 0.857 with accuracy 0.775.

The direct terms each raise the risk (per standardised unit: age 0.79, smoker 0.40, BMI 0.38, creatinine 0.36, diabetes 0.28, noise column 0.17); systolic blood pressure and heart rate have no connections.

Sodium acts through three hinges (switch-on points from typical-case sweeps): a low-sodium arm that switches on between sodium 135 and 134 mmol/L (lower for higher BMI) and rises steeply as sodium falls, a first high-sodium hinge that switches on between 137 and 138 and rises gently (slightly more f

In the typical case the whole-model risk is 77% at sodium 130, 10% at 137 and 92% at 145; switching the sodium structure off lowers AUC from 0.857 to 0.697, the six direct terms together from 0.857 to 0.767.

Two further three-unit chains driven by the noise column (one switched off by diabetes, one by high creatinine) feed small negative terms into the low-sodium arm; together they are worth AUC 0.8565 against 0.8532 and are described, not explained.

The two noise chains (units 881_a, 6957, 8692 and 881_b, 7171, 8285) are described by their closed forms but have no clinical reading: their main input is the random noise column, and they change whole-model AUC only from 0.8565 to 0.8532 (mean risk change -0.0072).

The concept probe's best library concepts are 'sodium * noise' for the first (score 0.79) and the gating input 'creatinine' for the second (score 0.91); these grades overstate their meaning, since neither concept names what the chain does to the prediction.
The edge from the low-sodium arm into the first high-sodium hinge (weight 0.0087) is kept for function preservation but is inert on the training rows (0 rows with both units positive).
The small direct noise-column term (weight 0.17) is fitted noise.
